text: A huge share of enterprise data — PDFs, scanned forms, contracts, invoices — sits outside any table, unqueryable by SQL. Agent Bricks is Databricks' umbrella for AI building blocks like this; their Document Intelligence pattern turns a folder of raw PDFs into governed, structured Delta tables, incrementally, using two SQL functions.

ai_parse_document takes a raw document and extracts its content — text, tables, layout structure. ai_extract takes that parsed content plus a described schema and pulls out specific typed columns, like invoice number or line-item totals. Parse first to get usable content, then extract the fields your downstream use case actually needs.

This isn't a new architecture — it's the exact Bronze, Silver, Gold pattern from Chapter 3, applied to unstructured files. Bronze holds raw document bytes via Auto Loader. Silver is a streaming table built incrementally with ai_parse_document. Gold is a streaming table built incrementally with ai_extract against a declared schema. New documents flow through automatically, the same as any other Declarative Pipeline.

Once the pipeline exists, Databricks' own reference pattern wires it into a three-task Lakeflow Job: Auto Loader ingests raw documents into Bronze, the Declarative Pipeline runs to produce Silver and Gold, and a downstream dashboard refreshes against the new Gold table — the exact same depends_on fan-out pattern from Chapter 4.
